paper_title: TL;DR Too Long, Do Re-weighting for Effcient LLM Reasoning Compression
caption: Comparison of accuracy and generation length between Vanilla CoT and our method on four benchmark datasets (GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, AMC) using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen models. consistently reduces generation length while maintaining or improving accuracy across both 7B and 14B model scales.

model_annotations.English: The bar chart titled "DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B Generation Length Comparison" illustrates the generation length (in words) for two methods—Vanilla CoT (light pink bars) and TLDR (Ours, dark red bars)—across four benchmark datasets: GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, and AMC. The vertical axis represents generation length, scaled linearly from 0 to 8000 words, with tick marks at 1000-word intervals. The horizontal axis lists the four datasets in left-to-right order. For each dataset, two bars are grouped side-by-side: the light pink bar corresponds to Vanilla CoT, and the dark red bar represents TLDR (Ours). The chart shows that TLDR consistently reduces generation length compared to Vanilla CoT. Specific values are annotated above each bar: for GSM8K, Vanilla CoT generates 679 words while TLDR produces 200 words (a -65% reduction); for MATH500, the values are 2951 and 2000 words (a -31% reduction); for AIME, the values are 6701 and 6400 words (a -4% reduction); and for AMC, the values are 4584 and 3800 words (a -16% reduction). The percentage reductions are labeled in red above each TLDR bar, indicating the relative decrease in generation length. The bars are not sorted by value but follow the fixed order of the datasets on the x-axis. No visual emphasis such as outlines or shading distinguishes any particular dataset or method beyond the default color coding.
model_annotations.German: The bar chart titled "DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B Generation Length Comparison" illustrates the generation length (in words) for two methods—Vanilla CoT (light pink bars) and TLDR (Ours, dark red bars)—across four benchmark datasets: GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, and AMC. The vertical axis represents generation length, ranging from 0 to 8000 words with linear, evenly spaced tick marks at intervals of 1000. The horizontal axis lists the four datasets in left-to-right order. For each dataset, two adjacent bars are shown: the light pink bar corresponds to Vanilla CoT, and the dark red bar corresponds to TLDR (Ours). The chart indicates that TLDR consistently reduces generation length compared to Vanilla CoT, with percentage reductions labeled above each dark red bar: -65% for GSM8K (Vanilla CoT: 679 words, TLDR: ~200 words), -31% for MATH500 (Vanilla CoT: 2951 words, TLDR: ~2030 words), -4% for AIME (Vanilla CoT: 6701 words, TLDR: ~6430 words), and -16% for AMC (Vanilla CoT: 4584 words, TLDR: ~3840 words). The bars are arranged in groups by dataset, and the reduction percentages are visually emphasized in red text above the TLDR bars. The chart demonstrates that TLDR achieves shorter outputs across all datasets while maintaining or improving accuracy, as stated in the caption.
